evidence: Dimension weights: tests/scoring.toml:5-8 functional 0.6 / polish 0.2 / visual 0.2, gates 0.0 (lines 1-3), functional floor 0.05 (lines 10-11). The file and tests/tools/score.py are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff clean) and match the skill delivery profile (SKILL.md:28) and the internal workbook annotation E45 (functionality 60 percent). score.py:46 computes sum(w*score)/sum(w), so functionality carries 60 percent and the two non-functional dimensions together are capped at 0.40; no weight key sits in any [judge] block. Per-criterion weights (parsed with tomllib): functional has 42 binary criteria, total weight 58.5, values 1.0 x15, 1.5 x21, 2.0 x6 (ratio at most 2:1). The 2.0 items are the hardest and most brief-central behaviours: cw_multi_caret_typing_atomic (functional/judge.toml:96-99), cw_same_line_carets (114-117), cw_js_format_semantics_and_undo (186-189), cw_last_good_recovery (285-288), cw_stop_cancels_pending_work (303-306), cw_live_update_keeps_editing_state (384-387). The 1.0 items are the simpler single-surface behaviours (typing/join 24-27, caret navigation 33-36, mouse selection 51-54, find 132-135, basic run 213-216, HTML preview 222-225, console order 267-270). By area: editor 28.0 (47.9 percent), runtime/preview 19.5 (33.3 percent), saved snippets/concurrency 11.0 (18.8 percent), which follows instruction.md:1 ('The editor itself matters ... format it, make changes in several places, and then run it ... without losing a draft when another tab saves first'). The closest thing to style inside functional, the two syntax-colouring criteria (168-171 at 1.5, 177-180 at 1.0), is 2.5/58.5 = 4.3 percent of the dimension and is not weighted above behaviour of comparable difficulty. No functional, polish or gate criterion reads source or grades structure. Polish: 6 binary criteria at 1.0 each (polish/judge.toml:21,30,39,48,57,66). Visual: 3 likert criteria, points 5, 1.0 each (visual/judge.toml:22,38,54). Gates: 3 binary criteria under all_pass, no reward mass. Sanity check of the non-functional maximum: a submission that passes both gates and only just clears the floor (functional must exceed 0.05, i.e. more than 2.925 of 58.5 weight, so at least two or three criteria) could reach at most about 0.03 + 0.40; in practice four of the six polish criteria need working Format, Undo/Redo, Replace all or Save (polish/judge.toml:32,41,50,59), so a dead app cannot collect the full polish share, while the visual 0.20 is collectable by appearance alone. That ceiling is fixed by the shared template policy, not by this task. Observation recorded, not a defect: because 42 functional criteria share 0.6 while 6 polish and 3 visual criteria share 0.2 each, the effective reward mass per criterion is 1.03 / 1.54 / 2.05 percent for functional weights 1.0 / 1.5 / 2.0, 3.33 percent per polish criterion and 6.67 percent per visual criterion (1.33 percent per likert point). So cw_undo_redo_availability (polish/judge.toml:45-48) is worth more than cw_stop_cancels_pending_work, and one visual likert point is worth more than cw_basic_run_output. This follows arithmetically from the mandated dimension split and the criterion counts; per-criterion weights cannot change a dimension total, and the template itself has the same shape. Counterexample attempts: (a) a good-looking app whose Run never works still loses the 19.5-weight runtime group plus the Run-dependent format criteria, about 0.22 of reward, far more than any polish or visual gain available; (b) a conforming, fully working but plain app loses at most part of the 0.20 visual share. Neither shows weight misdirected away from functionality. Run evidence: no configured judge run exists for these bytes. The hosted run on an earlier candidate (reward.json hash verified against the index) shows functional 1.0, polish 1.0, visual 0.9167, reward 0.9833 = 0.6 + 0.2 + 0.2 x 0.9167, which agrees with the weighting formula only; that candidate had 41 functional criteria, so it is not a measurement of the current per-criterion weights. This row is a static weight-design judgement and does not depend on a missing measurement.
